CHIEF COMPLAINT
Shortness of breath.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Lawrence is a 62-year-old male with past medical history significant for type 1 diabetes, congestive heart failure, depression, and reflux who presents with complaints of shortness of breath and swelling. Patient reports noticing swelling and attributes it to attending house parties and eating salty foods. He endorses feeling lethargic. Dyspnea is exertional, occurring with exertion such as walking up stairs. Symptoms began approximately 10 days ago. Patient reports mild leg swelling. He notes discomfort when lying flat in bed and feels stiff upon waking, requiring time to adjust when standing. Patient reports one episode of acute dyspnea at night approximately one week ago but states this has not recurred and he has not been concerned about it. Regarding diabetes control, patient reports blood sugars have been stable with good monitoring during the work week, though he admits sometimes forgetting to monitor on weekends. Denies recent spikes in blood glucose. Regarding depression, patient notes it has been a challenging year and a half. He has tried natural solutions including outdoor stretching in the summer and is not ready to start medications at this time but is open to suggestions. Regarding reflux, patient has been managing with lifestyle modifications including cutting back on Red Bull and caffeine. Alcohol intake has been reduced, particularly during the holiday season.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient endorsed shortness of breath on review of systems form. Denies chest pain, fever, chills, cough, or abdominal pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type 1 diabetes
Congestive heart failure
Depression
Reflux

MEDICATIONS
Insulin pump
Omeprazole

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works during the week and is busy on weekends. Enjoys chocolate bars. Attends house parties. Has been working on dietary modifications and reducing caffeine and alcohol intake. Previously used outdoor stretching as natural solution for depression management.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Good. Pulse oximetry: Good.
Neck: No jugular venous distension. No carotid bruits.
Heart: Slight 3 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur appreciated.
Lungs: Crackles appreciated bilaterally at the bases.
Lower extremities: 1+ pitting edema.

RESULTS
Chest X-ray: No evidence of airspace disease. No pneumonia.
Labs: No elevated white blood cell count.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Acute heart failure exacerbation: Start lasix 40 mg daily. Patient to weigh himself daily. Instructed to call if weight is not going down or if weight increases. Instructed to call or go to emergency room if shortness of breath worsens at rest, as patient may need intravenous diuretics.
2. Type 1 diabetes: Order hemoglobin A1c in approximately one month to assess need for adjustments. Follow up with endocrinologist. Ensure recent eye exam completed.
3. Depression: Refer to psychiatry for talk therapy. No medications at this time.
4. Reflux: Continue omeprazole 20 mg daily.
